title: Chirality-induced spin selectivity without intrinsic spin-orbit coupling: Role of current-induced molecular orbital moment
authors: Sumit Ghosh, Angela Wittmann, Frank Matthes, Daniel E. Bürgler
abstract: The microscopic origin of the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) in helical molecules remains an open question. Recent experiments suggest that a significant contribution to CISS arises from the molecule itself, which is disregarded in existing interfacial or scattering based theories. Here we present an alternative theory of CISS to address this molecular contribution. The mechanism is based on the circulation of charge current in molecular loops that generates a molecular orbital moment (MOM). The direction of the MOM is governed by the gauge field arising from the structural distortion of the molecule and is associated with the handedness of the molecule. Such a MOM can produce finite CISS magnetoresistance and magnetochiral conductance asymmetries that are even in bias voltage, without violating the Onsager-Casimir reciprocity relations. Depending on the Fermi level and bias voltage, the MOM can be controlled externally, which can result in additional crossings of the enantiomer $I-V$ curves. Finally we explain the origin of the electrical magnetochiral anisotropy within the same framework, which establishes its generic applicability.
summary: The paper proposes that Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) in chiral molecules originates from a current-induced Molecular Orbital Moment (MOM). This MOM arises from an effective gauge field associated with structural distortions, allowing the effect to be explained without invoking intrinsic spin-orbit coupling. The theory successfully predicts characteristic asymmetries in transport measurements like MChA.
main_problem: The paper addresses the unresolved microscopic origin of Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) in helical molecules, proposing a mechanism that accounts for intrinsic molecular contributions.
main_result: CISS can arise from a current-induced Molecular Orbital Moment (MOM), whose direction is governed by a gauge field linked to the molecule's structural handedness, all without requiring intrinsic spin-orbit coupling.
method: The theory models transport using a tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating a Peierls phase derived from bond length variations, and calculates observables via Green's functions.
model_or_system: The system uses chiral molecules like heptahelicene ($\chi^{\pm}[7]	ext{H}$), modeled by a tight-binding Hamiltonian. The mechanism centers on the generation of an emergent MOM due to circulating charge currents in molecular loops.
key_observables: Magnetochiral conductance asymmetry (MChA) and CISS magnetoresistance, I-V characteristics for enantiomers ($\chi^+$ vs $\chi^-$), and the Molecular Orbital Moment (MOM).
important_parameters: Bias voltage ($V_B$), external magnetic field ($B_{	ext{ext}}$), coupling parameters ($t_B, t_T$), and the gauge flux ($\Phi$).
main_assumptions: The theory builds upon incorporating a distortion-induced gauge field to satisfy Onsager-Casimir reciprocity relations and explain zero-bias crossings.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate I-V curves and MOM in enantiomers under bias/field, showing the influence of structural gauge fields ($\mathbf{A}_\chi$) on transport asymmetry. Later figures detail the decomposition of MOM into Fermi surface and sea contributions.
paper_structure: The paper develops a theoretical framework based on modifying the Hamiltonian with a Peierls phase derived from molecular distortion to generate an emergent MOM. It then calculates transport properties (I-V curves, MChA) using Green's functions, analyzing how this MOM dictates chirality effects in the absence of intrinsic SOC.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical mechanism for spin selectivity based purely on geometric and electronic structure effects (gauge fields/orbital moments), which is highly relevant to molecular spintronics and quantum transport phenomena studied in AMO physics.
